correctness.rationale: The explicit numerator P and positive denominator D satisfy the four collocation equations and initial condition; uniqueness follows by Gaussian quadrature energy positivity. The endpoint numerator is a sum of squares plus 60. Exact polynomial elimination gives discriminant 6048000*x^12*F(x^2), two positive simple F roots by Sturm variations 4→3→2, and an independent derivative-resultant certificate rules out triple roots there. Sturm time-root counts at x=1,6,12 prove the 0/2/4 open-interval census; signs at the algebraic Gauss nodes determine collision positions. The included exact symbolic verifier independently reproduces every critical computational identity and rational sign count; numerical roots are illustrative only.

value.rationale: Event detection within an accepted time step can report false crossings even when end-step values remain positive. The complete two-stage false-zero bifurcation and exact collision thresholds provide a mathematically motivated diagnostic for a standard stiff scalar test problem; the integrated-factor stage test gives a structural finite-sample nonnegativity criterion for scalar decay collocation at all stage counts. This is a sharp, exact scope-aware result rather than a small rounded improvement, and no general nonlinear significance is asserted.
